metas.name: Paterson
metas.description: Captures a routine life as a work of art. One week with a bus driver named Paterson, in Paterson, who writes poems about matchboxes and waterfalls between shifts.

metas.name: Tampopo
metas.description: Captures food as craft, sex, comedy and social ritual all at once. A truck driver mentors a widow until her ramen is perfect, cut with vignettes of people eating in every possible way.

metas.name: Do the Right Thing
metas.description: Captures a neighbourhood on the hottest day of the year. A Brooklyn block and a pizzeria wall of fame, everyone funny and aggrieved in their own direction until the heat does what heat does.

metas.name: Synecdoche, New York
metas.description: Captures a life trying to represent itself honestly, and drowning in the attempt. A theatre director builds a scale copy of his city inside a warehouse and keeps casting people to play people, including himself, for decades.

metas.name: Grey Gardens
metas.description: Captures a mother and daughter fused together in a decaying mansion. The Beales, relatives of Jackie Kennedy, singing, bickering and feeding raccoons in the attic — performing for the camera and trapped with each other.

metas.name: Dr. Strangelove
metas.description: Captures nuclear annihilation as a bureaucratic procedure. Generals, presidents and advisors in rooms — vain, procedural and insane — while the world ends by checklist.

metas.name: The Death of Stalin
metas.description: Captures absolute power as petty, terrified men improvising. Stalin drops dead and his inner circle plot, flatter and panic in the same breath — very funny, and people keep being shot between jokes.

metas.name: Withnail and I
metas.description: Captures the end of youth as squalor and one great friendship rotting. Two out-of-work actors in 1969 London, a disastrous country holiday, and one of them beginning to leave the other behind.

metas.name: Election
metas.description: Captures ambition so pure it becomes frightening, at a high school. A student election, a teacher who decides one candidate must be stopped, and everyone's voiceover giving their self-justifying version.

metas.name: Chungking Express
metas.description: Captures city loneliness at pop speed. Hong Kong, two lovesick cops, expired pineapple cans, and a snack-bar girl breaking into a man's flat to clean it while 'California Dreamin'' loops.

metas.name: Eighth Grade
metas.description: Captures social anxiety in the age of front-facing cameras, exactly. A girl filming confident advice videos she cannot follow, pool parties endured minute by minute, and a father scene near the end that rearranges parents.

metas.name: The Apartment
metas.description: Captures loneliness in a big company, and kindness as a decision. An insurance clerk lends his flat to executives for their affairs to get promoted, loves the elevator girl from afar, and hits Christmas at the lowest point of both.

metas.name: Amélie
metas.description: Captures a lonely young woman engineering small happinesses for strangers. Montmartre, a tin of childhood treasures returned to its owner, and a heroine who can fix everyone's life except ask for anything in her own.

metas.name: Singin' in the Rain
metas.description: Captures pure performed joy, inside a story about an industry panicking. Hollywood switching to sound, a star with a terrible voice, and musical numbers that still feel like showing off for the love of it.

metas.name: Paddington 2
metas.description: Captures decency as something contagious. A bear framed for stealing the pop-up book he wanted to buy his aunt, sent to prison — and the prison improves because he is in it.

metas.name: Big Night
metas.description: Captures two brothers arguing about whether a meal should be art or business. Italian immigrants, a failing restaurant, one elaborate dinner to save it, and a final wordless scene of one cooking breakfast for the other.

metas.name: Rushmore
metas.description: Captures a precocious teenager's grandiosity as a grief strategy. A scholarship kid who runs every club and stages huge plays falls for a widowed teacher and goes to war with a sad industrialist who is, emotionally, the same age.

metas.name: Day for Night
metas.description: Captures a film set as a chaotic temporary family. Truffaut plays the director of a mediocre melodrama, keeping affairs, breakdowns, accidents and deadlines moving toward a finished film nobody thinks is great and everybody needs.

metas.name: The Truman Show
metas.description: Captures a paranoia that turns out to be an accurate description. An insurance salesman in a seaside town so pleasant it feels laminated, a sky that malfunctions, and a dawning suspicion about everyone who loves him.

metas.name: Lady Bird
metas.description: Captures a mother and daughter who love each other in a way that keeps missing. Sacramento, a girl desperate to leave for the East Coast, a mother working double shifts, fights in moving cars, and a final voicemail that reframes every argument.

metas.name: Secretary
metas.description: Captures kink as, for one specific person, a form of self-knowledge. A young woman fresh out of hospital for self-harm takes a typing job with a demanding lawyer, in a relationship the film treats as tender rather than a diagnosis.

metas.name: Touki Bouki
metas.description: Captures two young people dreaming of Paris so hard the film itself starts hallucinating. Senegal: a cowherd and a student steal and scheme toward a ship, on a motorbike with a skull mounted on it, in editing that jumps like a skipping song.

metas.name: Hyenas
metas.description: Captures a village discovering its price. A woman returns after decades, impossibly rich, offering her poor hometown a fortune for one act of 'justice' against the man who wronged her — while shops fill with goods bought on credit.

metas.name: Gummo
metas.description: Captures boredom and poverty in an American town as unconnected afternoons. Xenia, Ohio, after a tornado: kids sniffing, selling dead cats, taped monologues, no plot arriving to save anyone.

metas.name: Daisies
metas.description: Captures two girls deciding the world is spoiled, so they'll be spoiled too. A Czech New Wave food-fight against everything — banquets wrecked, scissors, fire, a chandelier swing — anarchy as pure visual mischief.

metas.name: Playtime
metas.description: Captures modern architecture failing to be lived in. Tati wanders a Paris of glass and identical cubicles where the jokes happen at the edges of the frame, all at once, none of them underlined.

metas.name: The Long Goodbye
metas.description: Captures a decent man out of sync with his decade. Altman's Philip Marlowe shuffles through sunlit, corrupt Los Angeles in a rumpled suit, the last person still taking loyalty seriously.

metas.name: It's Such a Beautiful Day
metas.description: Captures a mind coming apart, drawn with stick figures. Hertzfeldt narrates a man with a failing brain in three chapters — funny, fragmented, and by the end genuinely cosmic.

metas.name: Toni Erdmann
metas.description: Captures a father trying to joke his daughter back to life. A prankster dad with false teeth infiltrates his consultant daughter's sterile Bucharest existence — a comedy that keeps tipping into grief and back.

metas.name: The Favourite
metas.description: Captures court power as intimate warfare. Two women compete to be Queen Anne's favourite — her bed, her ear, her rabbits — through fisheye candlelit corridors, with a lonely, raging queen at the centre.

metas.name: The Worst Person in the World
metas.description: Captures turning thirty with every option still open and none chosen. Oslo in twelve chapters: a woman cycles through careers and men, including a night that pauses the entire city so she can test a life before living it.

metas.name: The Banshees of Inisherin
metas.description: Captures being dumped by a friend. One morning Colm simply doesn't want to talk to Pádraic anymore, and a whole island watches a small rejection escalate toward the mythic. Funny, until the exact moment it isn't.

metas.name: Crumb
metas.description: Captures how the same upbringing produces a famous artist, a broken man, and something in between. Cartoonist R. Crumb and his two brothers, all shaped by one brutal household, in Terry Zwigoff's unsparing family portrait.

metas.name: American Movie
metas.description: Captures delusion and genuine talent living in the same person. Mark Borchardt, a Wisconsin sanitation worker with debts and a drinking problem, tries to finish a horror short to fund his dream feature — very funny until, suddenly, it isn't.

metas.name: Man Bites Dog
metas.director: Rémy Belvaux, André Bonzel, Benoît Poelvoorde
metas.description: Captures the complicity problem pushed to its logical endpoint — the cluster's one fiction: a student crew follows a charming serial killer for a documentary, graduating from filming him, to holding the camera steady, to helping.

metas.name: Sherman's March
metas.description: Captures the personal documentary being invented out of failure. McElwee sets out to film Sherman's Civil War campaign, gets dumped before shooting starts, and the film becomes his disastrous search for love among old flames, narrated in a deadpan spiral.

metas.name: Time of the Gypsies
metas.description: Captures folk storytelling surviving, barely, inside modern crime. A Romani teenager with telekinetic powers is lured into a smuggling life in Italy, half narrated by Goran Bregović's score — Petrović's world taken into magical realism.

metas.name: Ten Canoes
metas.description: Captures oral tradition's actual structure. In Arnhem Land, an elder tells a young man a cautionary ancestral tale inside which another tale is told, while they hunt goose eggs in the swamp — stories nested for a practical moral purpose, with jokes.

metas.name: Amarcord
metas.description: Captures a community remembering itself, every ritual half affection and half mockery. Fellini rebuilds his hometown of Rimini as permanent carnival: fascist rallies, family dinners, a peacock in the snow, a whole town rowing out to greet an ocean liner.

metas.name: Calendar
metas.description: Captures diaspora as a loop of beautiful images you can't live inside. Egoyan sends a Canadian photographer to Armenia to shoot twelve ancient churches for a calendar, his marriage failing in the car between sites — then the ritual repeats, reframed, back in Toronto.
